From: Kimberly Cho <kim.cho@aperturehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Aperture Health case study — please review cost numbers

Priya —

Appreciate the draft. Overall it looks great. A couple of quick items from our side:

- The 62% figure for per-token cost reduction is correct when comparing our previous managed endpoint spend to Redwood Dedicated after enabling KV caching and INT8 quantization; please add the qualifier "after enabling KV caching and INT8 quantization".
- The p95 latency numbers are correct for our standard conversation workload, but for long-context transcripts (>") 2k tokens) the p95 is closer to 420–460ms; suggest phrasing: "median p95 latency for typical chat sessions dropped from ~420ms to ~170ms; longer transcript workloads remained in the 420–460ms range."
- We prefer to soften the quote slightly — remove the phrase "transformed our backbone" and replace with "meaningfully improved our inference reliability and cost profile."

I've attached a PDF with inline comments (redlines) for small editorial notes.

Attachment: Aperture_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 14KB)

Can you also confirm the draft doesn't call out our exact monthly token volumes? We prefer an anonymized band ("~hundreds of millions of tokens/month").

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Cho
Director of Engineering, Aperture Health
kim.cho@aperturehealth.com

Team —

Thanks for the ping. Quick legal guidance below:

- Use the anonymized token language: "~hundreds of millions of tokens/month" is fine; do not include exact monthly figures without a signed data-sharing addendum.
- The qualifier for the 62% reduction is important — add language that these are "measured after enabling KV caching and INT8 quantization on Redwood Dedicated and may vary by workload."
- Regarding the softened quote: approve the proposed replacement language from Kim.
- Please remove any statement that implies we guarantee identical results for other customers; instead use "customer-reported results" and cite the interview date (Aug 24, 2026).

If the customer provides a signed publication waiver or form, we can include fuller specifics later. Otherwise, follow the conservative edit.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
